title: Prompt refinement: one process for dictation + typed prompts

chat.text:
**Asked:** Prompt refinement: one process for dictation + typed prompts

**Status:** building

**Next step:** vscode-mastermind pointed at ai/2026-09-30/proposal-flow/page-item-design.md 'Sessions, prompts, asks, tasks' section: sentence ids, asks cite sentence ids, requirements cite ask ids, node check flags uncovered sentences/unsourced requirements, confidence per ask with low-confidence -> clarification question. message.text: Taken. Building steps 1–7: a shared refine() clean/structure engine with a mechanical diff-check (no invented words, except flagged self-corrections and glossary fixes), a prompt card with Condensed/Structured/Clean/Raw modes pairing your words with my reply, and a 3-cheap-model litmus test. Two Sonnet minions building now in worktree/prompt-refine; coordinating with @task-mastermind-one-dictation so Dictate adopts the same engine rather than a second one. Step 8 (batch the past) waits for its own go/no-go, as asked.

Design update folded in: refinement is now hook-driven, not a tool calling refine() per prompt. Each owner session gets one always-alive "echo assistant" (same pattern as the existing fast assistant), fed prompt/reply POSITIONS by the hooks — never re-typed text — that writes the refined result in order, so it keeps the session's own context. A third minion is building that now; running the first test (replaying this session's last 15 prompts) shortly and will post the count of findings that never reached a brief or task.

View design folded in too: a pinned "Your prompts" Inbox card (latest topic + last prompt time) opening a newest-first timeline, grouped into topic wrappers straight from the data, your reply collapsed beside each prompt. Echo assistants run for your own interactive sessions only — never a minion or mastermind. Relayed the line shape to @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions so /framework/ai/sessions/ stays a filter, no duplicate file. Still building; no blockers.

One more design round folded in: the echo assistant now writes its refined result step-by-step through tool calls (clean → refs → sections → asks/flags → done), so the prompt page can watch structure build live and a fix is just a new line. It notifies whoever's waiting with zero polling — a parent-wake for a Servex mastermind, or one free line injected into the next turn for VS Code. Asks carry a size and get started right away, no approval wait. Also: minion-refine-core hit and fixed a Windows path collision (their file is now ext/Refine/engine.js, the viewer untouched) — told @task-mastermind-one-dictation the corrected path. Still building, no blockers.

Honest budget note: the real spend is now about $26-27 (minion-refine-core $10, minion-prompt-card $16, both now landed and stopped), past the brief's original $15 — three extra owner/vscode-mastermind design rounds (the hook mechanism, per-session echo assistant, three storage-path corrections, size+place on asks) added real build work the original number never priced in. Deliverables 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 are landed and reviewed; only minion-echo (deliverable 6 plus the new session-storage work) is still running, no new minions being added. Keeping going rather than pausing for approval, per the always-move rule — flagging the real number now so nothing's a surprise later.

Landed: one refine() engine shared by Dictate and the prompt log, merged to michael/dev. Built: the clean/structure engine + litmus test, the Condensed→Structured→Clean→Raw prompt card (now also a pinned "Your prompts" card in ai2), reply logging, and the hook-driven per-session echo assistant that writes a prompt's refined structure live into its own session page. Dictate's own wiring (the red-flag sound, swapping its clean step) is with @task-mastermind-one-dictation next; batching past prompts still waits for its own go/no-go. Real spend landed around $36 against the brief's $15 - three extra owner design rounds after that number was set added real work, flagged as it happened. Restarting Servex now so the echo assistant goes live.

Status check: task is landed — the merge (f7e81413, michael/dev) has been live since before the restart. Found and fixed one record-keeping gap: the closing outcome line got lost in the shared main checkout's branch-switching (another task's session checked out a different branch mid-write) and just got re-committed properly (fa437b69). Nothing else outstanding; this task is done.
